name: Closed-Stance Transfer
execution: Curtsy RDL + Cable Rotational Chop (Explosive, No Pause)
swap: Cross-Behind Lunge + Med Ball Rotational Throw

manual.why: TAG CLEANUP ONLY - the biomechanical problem is NOT fixed and is still queued. Dead 'Cable' tag was really a naming problem: the execution said only 'Paloff Chop' and a Pallof can be band or cable, so the cable is now named. Med Ball appears only in the swap and moves to swap_equipment. STILL OPEN: the focus and name promise a rotational transfer, but the rotational movement is a Pallof hold, so nothing actually accelerates the torso. That is the filter 1 issue raised in the audit and it needs a separate supersede. || FILTER 1 FIX. Audit reasoning, as recorded on id 128: 'the focus and name promise a rotational transfer, but the rotational movement is a Pallof hold, so nothing actually accelerates the torso.' A Pallof press is a resisted anti-rotation hold - the torso decelerates against the cable rather than accelerating, so a record called Closed-Stance Transfer promised a transfer it never trained. The chop is now a whip rather than a hold, driving up and across the diagonal with no pause, which is what actually accelerates the trunk. The med-ball throw deliberately stays in the SWAP: a rotational throw is the truest acceleration analogue for a tennis serve, and filter 1 forbids mimicking the sport skill under load, so the primary builds the raw quality with a cable and the athlete expresses it on court. Equipment and swap_equipment are unchanged and still pass the inversion check (one reserved implement primary against one common-tier swap).

name: Wide Ball Recovery
execution: Deep Lateral Lunge to Stick (2s, bodyweight) + Crossover Shuffle Recovery 3 Steps into Set Position
swap: Lateral Step to Stick (2s) + Lateral Shuffle Recovery 3 Steps into Set

manual.why: After a wide ball, the real work is stopping and getting home. || CLUNK-TEST READABILITY FIX - FLAGGED, THIS ONE IS WEAK. I could not recover the original audit rationale for id 79; it is not recorded in the record, so unlike ids 123 and 130 I am re-deriving rather than quoting. What I can defend: the execution ends in 'Immediate Crossover Run Back', which reverses direction straight out of a static 2s stick. Filter 2 asks for a reset step between a movement and its reversal, and a static hold is arguably not a step. The stronger objection is sporting rather than structural - a crossover run at full speed is not how a tennis player actually recovers; they shuffle and set. So the return becomes a shuffle into a set position, which is both a reset and the real skill shape, and the swap drops the crossover for a plain lateral shuffle so the two are genuinely different movements. If your audit flagged 79 for something else, tell me and I will redo this against the real concern - I would rather flag a weak fix than invent a violation to justify it.
manual.cue: Stretch wide, stop dead, then cross over and get home.

name: Trophy-Pose Coil & Brake
execution: Tall Kneeling Overhead Cable Triceps Extension (1s concentric, 4s eccentric) with Ribs Down
swap: Heavy Banded Overhead Triceps Extension (Slow Eccentric)

manual.why: MECHANICAL DATA FIX - NO COACHING CHANGE. This record had the same folding defect as ids 30, 51 and 60: ['Band'] was used only in the swap text but was folded into `equipment` instead of `swap_equipment`. The tag was not dead - it genuinely names an implement this drill needs - so it never tripped the dead-tag warning; it just sat in the wrong field, where it made the primary look like it needed a scarce tool it does not use, and it hid the split from filter 3 review. Correct split: `equipment` ['Cable', 'Band'] -> ['Cable'], `swap_equipment` None -> ['Band']. Execution, swap, focus, loading and rest are unchanged - the movement is identical and only the tag fields differ. Checked against the inversion check before writing: the swap needs 1 implement against the primary's 1, and the swap's implement is common-tier, so it is not trading a scarce tool for a cheaper one. Filter 3 intent is unchanged and now legible: comparing the two lists shows the swap drops the scarce implement, which is what the folded version could not express.
